artworks.title: 《无形之形》 Formless Form
artworks.intro: 空间中用肉眼看，没有作品。用我们今天观看世界的“主要方式” 手机或者IPAD屏幕看那片空间，有一个撑满空间的大铁球，观众举着手机通过调整自己与作品的距离和角度来观看作品的局部或者整体。于此同时，观众扫描二维码给手机按上准备好的软件，通过纸媒或者网络传播，让更多的人足不出户就可以在家里360度观看这件雕塑作品。Space with the naked eye, no works. We use the "main way" of viewing the world today, mobile phone or IPAD screen to look at that space, there is a big iron ball that fills the space, and the audience holds the mobile phone to watch the part or the whole of the work by adjusting the distance and Angle between themselves and the work. At the same time, the audience can scan the QR code and press the prepared software on the mobile phone to spread through the paper media or the Internet, so that more people can watch the sculpture in 360 degrees at home without leaving the house.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
张增增的《无形之形》完成于2014年，正值VR、AR、MR讨论大热的时期，是另一件元宇宙这一概念的先导性作品。艺术家在讨论数字世界无形的入侵关系，是对城市景观的介入，也是对数字时代到来的担忧。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张增增的作品《无形之形》，是接续关系。数字化的风景，与真实的风景和人，构成了一个整体。《无形之形》是未来的预言之一，尝试改变现在的，也恰是来自未来的想象力。

希望张增增的作品，能让你试着思考如何在未来生活，一切图像的真实和虚拟，也许会合而为一，你会有数字分身，会在不同的场景中，跳入跳出。如同科幻作品中，探讨的时空旅行者的困境，因为过度兴奋，可能会让你失眠。

The artist explores the intangible invasion of the digital world, intervening in urban landscapes and expressing concerns about the advent of the digital age.

artworks.title: 《大字》
artworks.intro:
从谷歌地图中位于新疆东部一处无人区的距离地面 10 公里的空中，可以 俯瞰到有 30 个巨大的中国字和 1 个感叹号盘桓在荒凉的戈壁上，每个字有一个 足球场那么大。这些大字是一些文革的口号，由碎石堆砌而成，在 1968 年这 里修建了一个秘密的军用机场，这些大字就是这个机场的航标。摄影机在这些 大字中穿行，在碎石堆积而成的乌托邦的幻觉里浮现出 1968 年世界各地的革 命浪潮，一些浪潮在开始，一些浪潮被熄灭⋯⋯ 
     Using Google Maps, one can look down from ten miles above upon a no-man’s land in eastern Xinjiang and see thirty enormous Chinese characters and an exclamation point twisting their way through the desolate Gobi Desert. Each character is the size of a football field and they form slogans from the Cultural Revolution, built with crushed stone. A secret military airport was built in just this spot in 1968, and these big characters served as its navigational markings. The camera makes its way through the characters, and there in the Utopian hallucination of the piled stones, the tidal wave of revolution that swept across the world in 1968 appears. Some waves were just beginning, while others were being extinguished....

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
雎安奇的《大字》完成于2015年，巨大的词句来自毛泽东先生的诗词，而这些诗词却在60年代作为军用，尤其是飞行员的航标。作品揭示一个时代的变化，尤其是技术升级之后，人在技术环境中，位置和身份的消逝。艺术家试着将当代艺术在同一时间探索的问题，与中国时间同步，让作品更深度的介入到地缘环境中，不同组织和文化环境中的人。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于雎安奇的作品《大字》，是历史维度的，由人贯穿的，巨大风景中的人之回响。此作品对时代、人和技术的反思，也可以被看作通往未来元宇宙的道路。

希望雎安奇的作品，能让你将今天的现实，放在过去的、历史的维度中，思考过去和现在。艺术家带我们去的无人之境，遗落的基地，那些曾经留下痕迹人。也许现在的时代，在地球的某处存在的人。是否也可能会在元宇宙的世界中，与你相遇。

Ju Anqi's "Big Characters" was completed in 2015, featuring massive words and phrases taken from the poetry of Chairman Mao Zedong. Interestingly, these poetic texts were used as military symbols in the 1960s, particularly for pilots. artworks.title: 键盘侠菩萨 Keyboard Man Bodhisattva
artworks.intro:
怪力乱神出自《论语》，“子不语怪力乱力乱神。”这句话在当下有很多种解析，最为学术界所认同的解释应当是，孔子不谈论不在神谱上的鬼神。怪力乱神从字面意思亦指关于怪异、勇力、叛乱、鬼神之事。

这个项目延续了张晓对中国民间社会的持续关注。张晓之前的很多作品都是源自故乡，是围绕着民间的美学和审美对民间社会进行深入的探讨，而这次的创作则从故乡的农村扩展到了更大范围的中国乡村社会，去关注这些形式丰富的民间信仰。这些新造的神像千奇百怪，同时他们的形象也涉及到这个时代的各行各业，这些源于当下的塑像形象打破了宗教原有的信仰和审美体系，转而变成了老百姓需要什么就会塑一个与之对应的菩萨。

张晓并非在批判这种民间信仰和艳俗的形象，他更多的是去呈现这种当下的存在。这种民间信仰在中国的乡村社会极为普遍，或许这些民间信仰并不能代表一种宗教，或者说这是宗教在中国的经济发展过程中所产生的一种变异，他们大都是生硬和直接的，更多的是体现出一种民众的集体无意识。这也是民间底层社会对于宗教和信仰的需求，他们渴望从这里寻求心理安慰和心理暗示。这些神像给他们提供了一个粗糙又直白的载体，藉此希望找到生活的出口。尽管这些菩萨或许并不在神谱之上，亦为很多人避而不谈之事。

Guai Li Luan Shen (‘怪力乱神’) stems from a line in the Analects of Confucius, “The subjects on which the Master did not talk, were: extraordinary things, feats of strength, disorder, and spiritual beings.” (‘子不语怪力乱力乱神’). There are many interpretations of this quotation today, but the most scholarly would be that Confucius did not talk about ghosts and gods that were not on the divine list. In a literal sense, the phrase Guai Li Luan Shen also refers to things about bizarreness, courage, rebellion as well as ghosts and gods.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
张晓的《键盘侠菩萨》是这几年，艺术家与木雕匠人合作的作品。类似《美国众神》（American Gods, 2001）小说中描述的，旧神被新神取代。彩塑的木雕则来自特别细微的日常需求，如《键盘侠菩萨》是否应该保佑那些驰骋网络的意见者？

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张晓的作品《键盘侠菩萨》，是日常而温情的，类似微小精神需要的具体化。而艺术家试着代入不同人群的价值观，及其信仰。

希望张晓的作品，能让你关注到文化和社群的多样性，进入到不同社群的视野，想象一下，一起进入到未来元宇宙的，也可能是人类整体，因相互补偿而共存。

Zhang Xiao's "Keyboard Man Bodhisattva" is a collaborative artwork between the artist and woodcarvers in recent years. Similar to the depiction in the novel "American Gods" (2001), where the old gods are replaced by new gods, the colorful wooden sculptures in this artwork stem from specific and subtle daily needs. For example, should the "Keyboard Man Bodhisattva" bless those who express their opinions freely on the internet?

artworks.title: 《异场》Different Field
artworks.intro:
棕丝为材料的装置作品是我一直持续到现在的一个系列，从选材到制作是一个漫长的过程，将棕榈叶片撕成棕丝，制作成一系列的生活物品，细看这些物品是一些“残缺”“非正常”的生活之物，作品以一种“未完成”的状态呈现出一个唯美与诗意的现场，背后却是廉价与平俗，正如理想与现实。在每一次与材料接触的过程都像是进行一场博弈，在控制与放任之间拿捏分寸，我试图让自己达到一种由技入道的状态，将“重”隐藏在“轻”之下。The installation works made of palm silk are a series that I have been working on until now. From material selection to production, it is a long process. Palm leaves are torn into palm silk and made into a series of daily objects.
Behind it is cheap and common, just like ideal and reality.
In every process of contact with materials is like a game, between control and laissez-faire, I try to let myself reach a state of technology into the road, the "heavy" hidden under the "light".

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
李娜的《异场》是艺术家十几年长期工作的线索，丝线状态下，显现出的任何形态，都可以被看作建筑的空间和场域。艺术家《异场》，还在讨论一些似是而非的关系，那些被确认为女性主义，或女性艺术特征的东西，也可以被看作文化异化的场域。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于李娜的作品《异场》，有着巨大的能量，时间流逝中，艺术家选择不懈的工作。在反向思考材料和时间的意义，反向思考性别和生命维度的意义。

希望李娜的工作，能让你重拾材料和美的认识，让日常的每一刻，都是劳作和努力的美感。

Li Na's "Different Field" is a culmination of the artist's long-term work spanning over a decade. Under the state of silk threads, any form that emerges can be regarded as the spatiality and domain of architecture. In her work "Different Field," the artist also explores some paradoxical relationships, where things identified as feminist or bearing characteristics of women's art can also be seen as fields of cultural estrangement.

artworks.title: 红、黄、蓝的构成生成器 Composition Generator in Red, Yellow, and Blue
artworks.intro:
《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》是一件通过代码模拟皮特·蒙德里安《红、黄、蓝的构成》创作的，探索色彩与形状无限组合可能性的数字艺术作品。

作品基于迭代分割、随机性与概率权重等基本数学原理创作，每次页面访问都会即时生成新的构图，确保每位收藏者获得的版本都是独一无二的。该作品限量发行1万份。此作品于2012年创作，作为我在伦敦大学金匠学院运算艺术专业中艺术家编程课程的一个项目，它反映了我在编程和创意表达方面的早期探索。蒙德里安生成器也是很多 Processing 创意编程课的一个阶段作业。

为本次展览及BTC区块链销售，我将作品由 processing 1.5版本升级至 p5.js。p5.js是加密艺术和生成艺术在Artblocks平台上最广泛使用的编程库。

"The Composition Generator of Red, Yellow, and Blue" is a digital art piece inspired by Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Yellow, and Blue." It explores the infinite possibilities of color and shape combinations using code. The artwork is based on fundamental mathematical principles such as iterative division, randomness, and probability weights, generating new compositions with each page visit. The artwork is code-based, while the artwork being exhibited and sold is a unique recorded version.

This work was created in 2012 as part of a project for the Artist Programming course in the Computational Arts program at Goldsmiths, University of London. It reflects my early exploration in programming and creative expression. The Mondrian Generator has also become a common assignment in many Processing creative programming courses.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
周姜杉的作品《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》，是一件基于网络生成的艺术创作，完成于2012年。作品探索生成的随机性，以及艺术历史的可变性。艺术家成为这一无限可能框架的设计者。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于周姜杉的作品《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》，是媒介更新后的再现，基于网络的、生成的，构成在加密线索中，更加永恒的新生。

希望周姜杉的作品，让你思考媒介批判的现实，如何认识到技术演化带来的更新，即是必然，也可能是有意识的选择。也许技术是你的朋友，你可以使用，并与之相处，让你的世界演化出多种可能。

Zhou Jiangshan's artwork "Composition Generator in Red, Yellow, and Blue" is a web-based generative art piece created in 2012. The work explores the randomness of generation and the variability of art history. The artist becomes the designer within this framework of infinite possibilities.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
董师的作品《gold、city dog、⚖️》，是一件长期的、每天的、基于网络的数字艺术创作。作品均来自艺术家董师每天的一张绘画。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于董师的作品《gold、city dog、⚖️》，是基于绘画媒介在数字生成过程的转化，是基于传播理论，在社群蔓延的艺术之转向。是现在我们都在经历的媒介化挑战的现实，我们会从今天向着未来继续前行。

希望董师的作品，让你愉快的，每天能有可能，出现在你的社群和朋友圈，电子化的瞬间，可能在回望的时候，没有了痕迹。试着理解人创造的，也都将消失。

artworks.title: Glass Memory
artworks.intro:
Glass Memory
动画
1’40”
2016

这件作品源于十多年前的一件用手持DV拍摄的习作，我用一个玻璃杯作为主角尝试了蒙太奇和长镜头的练习，直到其摔碎，那是我第一次接触到影像语言。现在这件习作已经丢失，留下的只有在我脑中零星模糊的几个画面，就像老DV的糟糕画质。<Glass Memory>是这件前作的“重制”，我试图从记忆的只言片语中挖掘更多的信息，但始终停留在某几个特定的画面上，想象似乎占据了主导，其余的记忆呈现出了一种中间状态，介于先验和日常，想象和记忆，虚拟和现实。就像光透过玻璃折射，水波泛起涟漪，你再看时，它们折叠、混合、扭动、异化出另一幅景象。

Glass Memory
Animation
1’40”
2016

This work can be traced back to an old work shot with a handheld DV more than ten years ago. The course of moving images brought me in contact with the language of film for the first time when I was in college. I made a work where a glass experienced a journey of “montage and long take” till smashing to pieces. The video has been lost only with some blurred images left in my mind，just like the poor images of the old DV. <Glass Memory> is a “resurrection” of the previous one. But the imagination dominates when I try to dig out more information from the fragments of memory. Only a few unstable mind images remain and the rest of memories show an in-between state living on the boundaries of transcendental experiences and daily lives, imagination and memories, virtual and actual. Just like light passing through glass and water rippling, when you look at them, they fold…

artworks.title: innumerable · jumping he
artworks.intro:
The term “innumerable” often connotes repetition, whether it is in reference to time, information, wealth, possibilities, or expressions of gratitude, longing, and love. In each case, “innumerable” implies a sense of repetition, which suggests that perseverance ultimately leads to permanence—a quality we often cherish in life. While we appreciate permanence and persistence, repetition itself is not always welcomed.

Yet, it is often through the most mechanical and rigid repetition that we notice subtle variations and shifts. Gilles Deleuze argues that repetition breeds difference, laying the groundwork for innovation. So, what lies ahead for the future of visual arts: repetition or innovation? Reflecting on the decades since my birth in the 1970s, I see few groundbreaking innovations aside from the Internet. Visual arts are rife with repetition. There is repetition in modes of expression, materials, styles, and even the underlying concepts portrayed in artworks. Becoming a professional in any field requires accruing experience, often gained through repetition. curator.text:
何见平的作品《innumerable》，是一件空间作品，在上海誌屋空间的外墙，随风而动。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于何见平的作品《innumerable》，也许是空间之间的流转，一种不可见自然力推动的世界，也许这是何见平对现在动荡中世界的暗喻，也指向不确定的未来。

希望你能亲身体验何见平作品的空间关系，能让这个微小的视频带着你的思绪，到一个去处，在随风流动的作品前，体会物件尺度和空间，的自然关系。

He Jianping's artwork "innumerable" is a spatial installation located on the exterior wall of the Shanghainese House space in Shanghai. It moves with the wind, creating a dynamic experience.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of He Jianping's work "innumerable" may represent the flow between spaces, a world propelled by invisible natural forces. artworks.title: MetaKaleidoscope
artworks.intro: The "Metakaleidoscope series" aims to explore the vast realm of visual effects, presenting a unique aesthetic experience characterized by its use of repetitive and symmetrical patterns. This exploration seeks to delve into the endless possibilities of how patterns can be arranged and perceived, pushing the boundaries of traditional visual aesthetics. By leveraging the concept of a kaleidoscope, which traditionally uses mirrors and pieces of colored glass to create ever-changing patterns when turned, this series likely transcends the physical limitations to explore more abstract or digitally enhanced visual experiences.

希望你能在刘真辰的作品中，体会循环往复的美，在这个《原万花筒》的世界缅怀你的童年。

artworks.title: MetaKaleidoscope_001
artworks.intro: The "Metakaleidoscope series" aims to explore the vast realm of visual effects, presenting a unique aesthetic experience characterized by its use of repetitive and symmetrical patterns. This exploration seeks to delve into the endless possibilities of how patterns can be arranged and perceived, pushing the boundaries of traditional visual aesthetics. By leveraging the concept of a kaleidoscope, which traditionally uses mirrors and pieces of colored glass to create ever-changing patterns when turned, this series likely transcends the physical limitations to explore more abstract or digitally enhanced visual experiences.

artworks.title: 直径 12.7
artworks.intro:
作品名称:直径 12.7 
影像 video 16:9 
作品简介: 在影像中出现的白碗实际直径是12.7厘米，而题目中只有数字没有单位。12.7的数字给观者留下的是一种想象，这种想象是以诗意对技术的一种消解。12.7可以无限大亦可以⽆无限小，其实无限大与无限小都是技术永远无法达到的。同时，这种对“无限”的想象如碗中的水，可见却又不可见。

Title: Diameter 12.7 
video 16:9 
Description: The actual diameter of the white bowl in the video is 12.7cm, but the title only contains a number and not a unit. 12.7 leaves the viewer with a kind of imagination, which is a kind of poetic dissolution of technology. 12.7 can be infinitely large or infinitely small, but in fact both infinity and infinity can never be achieved by technology. At the same time, this imagination of "infinity" is like water in a bowl, visible yet invisible.

artworks.title: Symphony No.1 - PAH
artworks.intro:
司马源作品
《Symphony No.1 – PAH》
声景，18’45”，2023

团队：
司马源（概念、作曲）
王晓建（医学诊断、数据采集）
卢明（后期音效制作）

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》为南京大学“万籁计划”艺术与声学跨学科驻地创作。

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》以一位患有罕见病“肺动脉高压(Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension，PAH)”的儿童的基因突变现象和临床表征，作为主要研究对象，借助声音媒介进行创作。将患者6方面的医学诊断结果进行数据可视化，包括将DNA、mRNA、 Protein序列的编码，以“映射（mapping）”规则，严格对应至不同音高；根据心脏超声影像的脉动规律，创作打击乐节奏；以及根据肺动脉导管检测波形图的峰值与谷值，用键盘弹奏旋律等。将每种诊断数据分别设置成一个特定的声部，并将“病变前后”的特征用不同音色表现，最终成曲。

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》，将使更多观众通过作品直观地了解疾病的潜在机制，也使不幸罹患肺动脉高压的人群得到关注。此外，本作品颠覆性地将遗传学与声学相结合，用“实验交响”的形式消解了人们对病痛的恐惧。同时，引发观者对生命、疾病和死亡，这一内在关系的思考与探索。

（注：本项目对儿童患者数据的使用已经监管人同意和授权；聆听本作品请佩戴耳机。）

curator.text:
司马源的作品《Symphony No.1 - PAH》，首先来自对病患和医疗系统的关注，如何将病患的信息转化为一件声音的作品。作品需要的声场还原度很高，需要一定的设备支持，才能获得最好的体验。

希望你能感受到司马源作品中的真诚之爱，对其他人的温情，以及技术带来跨越认知鸿沟的欣喜。也希望你能去这样发现，那些不能转化的知识，在未来能汇集成一个有趣的整体。

artworks.title: 水果立方表情/Fruit Cubic Emoticon
artworks.intro:
我们特地挑选了一些社交网络常见的水果表情符号，将其进行了马赛克效果处理后置入于一个立方体的六个面，随着立方体的不断旋转，水果表情符号也不断变化，从而构成了一个水果立方表情。我们将这个表情的塑造视为明天见组合一次探索二次元与三维边界的视觉造型实验，并希望透过其中一些代表深圳和南方特色的水果表情符号，向虚拟与现实边界越加模糊的今日世界传递一个明天见式的祝福。
We curated a selection of popular fruit emoticons from social media, applied a mosaic effect to them, and arranged them on the six faces of a cube. As the cube rotates, the fruit emoticons continuously change, thus constructing a fruit cubic emoticon. The emoticon-making is seeyoutomorrow’s experiment in visual plastic art, delving into the boundary between ACG and three-dimensional space. With emoticons of characteristic fruits in Shenzhen and South China, we attempt to extend a seeyoutomorrow-style greeting to today’s world, where the boundary between virtuality and reality is increasingly blurred.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
明天见的作品《水果立方表情》系列，来自于网络的表情符号，带有网络迷因文化（meme culture）基因，又类似哲学家说的“骰子一掷”。正是这两个因素构成了这系列作品的线索。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于明天见小组的创作，是游戏感的释放，轻描淡写的人生观。

希望你能感受到明天见小组的合作之轻松愉快，有时候艺术不一定有太多深意，有时候艺术也可以就是这样骰子一掷的痛快淋漓。

The artwork series "Fruit Cubic Emoticon" by the group "See You Tomorrow" draws from internet emoticons and carries the genetic code of meme culture. It also resembles what philosophers refer to as "throwing the dice." These two factors form the clues of this series.

artworks.title: From East Hellweg street to West Hellweg street（No.3）
artworks.intro: I engaged in conversations with the homeless on the streets of Germany and conducted 3D scans of them. Using digital information technology, I replicated their physical appearances. By examining their clothing, skin condition, and the items they carried, one can glean insights into their life experiences. Each person is born with a physical form, and as life circumstances and experiences change, so does the external manifestation of that form.

curator.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
curator.text:
张翀的《From East Hellweg street to West Hellweg street》系列，是技术和人的讨论，艺术家置自己于：社会内在运作，人的阶层现实，和人的物理形态之讨论中。最终作品如同巨大的偶戏中，可被穿戴的外壳。更进一步讨论，外在的差异，及其内在人性的冲突。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张翀存在着双重悖论，张翀设问的和社会实践的，恰是人类未来的困境。可被数据化的，可被拟态的，可被入侵的。艺术家形成这一过程的镜像关系，或隐于技术之后，却也在共享这一困境。

希望张翀的作品，能让你对人类有同情心，对自己的未来有希望，相信技术带来的，并非只有绝望，还有人类天性的游戏感，还有彼此映照的瞬间，拥抱科技，不放弃对人性的追问。

artworks.title: 言  ( chapter1)
artworks.intro:
言   以环境叙事的方法将AI学习人类语言的过程具象化为一场探索之旅。
玩家将成为懵懂的AI男孩深入人类的语言世界，以孩童般的视角感受不断弱化的语义和极端的语言如何一步步哺育AI男孩并最终将他塑造为一个“完整的人类”。
我们对语义通货膨胀的脉络发展、本质原因、以及未来影响进行研究梳理，使用AI自然语言处理模型-GPT3生成文本作为创作依据并运用游戏化设计的方法将其具象提取，以探索这场以AI为主角蓝本的数字叙事可能性。

artworks.title: Melting Myth 附行
artworks.intro:
当人造物初次突兀的在平原上伫立，我们的文明在蔓延和成长的同时，植物也在用他们的方式予以回应。他们以独特的，静谧的，温柔且有力的方式攀爬于我们的文明间，重新刻画我们的痕迹。自然与工业以不可逆的趋势彼此纠缠，或许他们之间不再是塑造与被塑造的关系，而是拥抱与被拥抱的温柔。作品通过记录和实验的方式探索自然与工业日益模糊的边界，以此反思以及想象二者可能的未来图景。
现代家庭植物培养基质中参杂了大量的工业甚至家装通用材质，此时，泥土不再是自然的泥土，人造物也不是自然的威胁，形成了一种源于日常的合成自然。我们现在所看到的环保与生态材料往往是由易降解为目的设计，而在现实中，混合的状态成为日常，甚至更优。作品试着提供一种新的视角去面对渗透日常生活的，人工与自然深度共生的可能。
